clues: This town is the chief town of its west shore province. It sits at the south tip of a big isle, off the west coast of its land.
Most of the year's rain falls in just four wet months, from November to February. Snow is rare, and some winters see none at all.
Settlers from Britain came here in 1843. The town took the name of their queen, and it is one of the old towns of the north-west shore.
Its old China town is the second most old in all of North America. Just one famed port town has one that is more old.
Two grand old sights mark this town: the house of laws by the port, and a vast old grand hotel from 1908.
